svg.title: Kafka low watermark: deletion waits for live replicas
svg.desc: Three snapshots of one partition with three live replicas: a leader on the left and two followers on the right. Initially every replica retains offsets 10 through 15 and has log start 10, so the low watermark is min(10, 10, 10), or 10. An administrative deletion request removes offsets below 13, keeping 13 itself. In the middle snapshot, the leader and replica-2 have advanced their log starts to 13, but live replica-3 still starts at 10. The low watermark remains min(13, 13, 10), or 10, and deletion is not complete even though the leader has already removed 10 through 12. In the final snapshot replica-3 also starts at 13, and the leader has learned this progress: the low watermark reaches 13 and deletion completes. Dashed slots labeled gone are unavailable history on the indicated replica. Blue vertical lines mark log starts. The low watermark tracks the minimum log start known to the leader across live replicas, not just the leader log start. Live followers count even outside the in-sync replica set. Consumer progress is independent of deletion, and physical segment reclamation can occur later.
svg.text: Kafka low watermark: deletion waits for live replicas
One partition, three live replicas. Log start = first available offset, marked by a blue line.
Low watermark = minimum log start known to the leader across the live replicas.

g.text: All three replicas retain offsets 10–15 and start at 10.
The planned cutoff is 13: remove 10–12 and keep 13–15.
The leader and replica-2 start at 13; live replica-3 still starts at 10.
Deletion incomplete: low watermark 10 still trails the leader’s log start 13.

svg.text: Replica-3 advances its log start to 13; the leader learns this progress.

g.text: All three replicas now start at 13; the leader has observed their progress.
Low watermark reaches the requested cutoff 13: deletion is complete.

svg.text: Live = broker considered alive by Kafka; a live follower outside the in-sync replica set (ISR) still counts.
Gone means logically unavailable. Consumer progress is independent; segment files may be reclaimed later.
